newsitem.title: USA: Kmart, Waban in talks on Builders Square.
newsitem.headline: Kmart, Waban in talks on Builders Square.

text.p: Kmart Corp, Waban Inc and Leonard Green & Partners LP, a private merchant banking firm, said they are discussing a transaction that would combine Kmart's Builders Square and Waban's HomeBase business to form a new home improvement company.

The talks are part of Kmart's plan to dispose of Builders Square, said Marvin Rich, executive vice president of strategic planning. The retailer intends to reclassify Builders Square as a "discontinued operation" in its year-end financial statements and record a net after-tax loss of $350 million to $400 million from discontinued operations.

If the transaction is completed, Los Angeles-based Leonard Green would hold the majority interest in what would become the nation's largest home improvement company, with Kmart and Waban each retaining minority interests.
The proposed new company would consist of about 250 stores in 25 states with annual revenues totaling nearly $4 billion.
Waban president Herbert Zarkin said his company has suspended activities related to a possible spinoff of BJ's Wholesale Club to allow time to consider the Kmart transaction.

"This transaction has the potential to provide Waban and its shareholders greater value than our previously announced plan to separate our BJ's Wholesale Club and HomeBase divisions through a tax-free spinoff of BJ's," Zarkin said in a statement.

"Should a sale of HomeBase be concluded as a result of these discussions, we would expect to use the proceeds to retire corporate debt and for general corporate purposes, including the repurchase of stock," Zarkin added.

Kmart's Rich said, "While we are in the preliminary stages of this transaction, all parties are interested in the potential opportunity that could come from combining these similar home improvement operations."
The proposed transaction is subject to completion of due diligence by all, arrangement of required bank financing and approval by the boards of Kmart and Waban.
Kmart has 2,141 Kmart and Super Kmart Centers. Builders Square operates 168 stores, primarily in the Midwest, with 1996 revenues expected to be more than $2.5 billion, the company said.

Natick, Mass.-based Waban is engaged in warehouse merchandising through its HomeBase and BJ's Wholesale Club businesses. HomeBase operates 84 stores in 10 states. BJ's Wholesale Club has 81 clubs in operation.
Kmart was up 1/8 to 11-1/4 and Waban up 3/4 to 27-7/8.
